question: Q-006
question_text: Single-copy RIFT rerun with conservative motion only
hypothesis: CASE-003 indicates the six-copy failure was initiated by a repeatable geometry/toolpath interaction that the C02-style 300/200 mm/s wall speeds and 10000/5000 mm/s^2 acceleration envelope amplified into local lift/deflection and nozzle contact. Reducing motion severity without changing geometry or filament should clear the common-Z failure region.
prediction: One RIFT object reaches full height without the repeated horizontal disturbance, raised extrusion, nozzle contact, or spaghetti seen in CASE-003. If it fails again at the same geometry/Z, the geometry/toolpath transition becomes the leading cause rather than the global motion envelope.
why_this_test: A single-copy rerun removes cross-object dragging as a confound and changes only the motion envelope. Filament, flow, temperatures, geometry, 0.20 mm layers, three walls, aligned seam, and the existing 120-132 mm Height Slowdown are held constant.
judge_on: Inspect the previously affected common-Z band first, then the full wall and end/channel features: no horizontal disturbance, raised/curling extrusion, nozzle-contact marks, spaghetti, or adhesion loss. Preserve photos even on a clean result.

notes: E-024 remains reserved for the v51/Kexcelled terracotta follow-up declared by E-023.
Do not change filament, temperatures, geometry, layer height, wall count, seam, or Height Slowdown for this run.
